dataset.title: Harmonized Terrestrial Plant-Arthropod Interaction Networks from Open Field Studies

abstract.para: A versioned synthesis of field-bounded terrestrial plant-arthropod feeding and host-association networks harmonized from openly accessible source datasets. Version 0.1.0 contains 346 network objects: 126 provisionally direct E0/E1 networks and 220 E2/E3 derived or extracted networks. Each network is delimited by place, sampling window, habitat, and protocol; evidence classes and dependency clusters allow transparent analytical subsets without changing the released corpus.

additionalInfo.para: Binary incidence is the cross-study representation. Quantitative source values remain in their original units and are not assumed comparable among studies. Blank cells are never converted automatically to biological zeros. Projected herbivore edges represent shared-host overlap and potential exploitative competition, not demonstrated realized competition.

CC0 applies to rights held by the synthesis creators in the harmonization, organization, metadata, and other original contributions. It does not supersede third-party rights or upstream dataset terms. Source-level licenses and required attribution are retained in sources.csv and derived_products.csv; in particular, the Shinohara et al. source-derived component remains subject to its upstream CC BY 4.0 attribution terms.

licensed.licenseName: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication

geographicCoverage.geographicDescription: Terrestrial field sites represented by the included studies in Brazil, Czech Republic, Japan, Mexico, Papua New Guinea, South Africa, United Kingdom, United States. Coordinates are retained only where supplied or explicitly documented by an upstream source.

purpose.para: Provide a citable, provenance-complete collection for computational ecology analyses of plant-herbivore bipartite networks and their shared-host herbivore projections, while keeping direct observations, repeated ecologies, derived networks, extracted layers, and metawebs explicitly separate.

gettingStarted.para: Begin with networks.csv, sampling_events.csv, and studies.csv to select ecology objects and account for dependence. Join interactions.csv for the canonical long-form edges and taxa.csv for source-local taxa. Use evidence_class, release_layer, independence_cluster_id, and the gate fields to construct a declared analytical subset. For stratified analyses, join networks.study_id to studies.study_id for source-provided ecosystem class, country, and field-system labels, and join networks.event_id to sampling_events.event_id for place, year, season or period, habitat, and protocol. These fields are selection and grouping variables rather than mandatory release filters. derived_products.csv, derivations.csv, sources.csv, and file_manifest.csv provide source and transformation provenance.

description.para: New source-derived components and corrections are released as explicit package revisions. Published revisions remain immutable and citable.

Search and screen candidate datasets under the locked rule that one network is one field-bounded ecology: place by sampling window by habitat by protocol. Repository location is a priority criterion, not a substitute for scientific eligibility.

Acquire immutable source files, verify registered SHA-256 hashes, parse source structures, preserve source-local taxon names and source values, and record every filtering and aggregation operation in derivations.csv.

Classify evidence as E0 direct bounded field ecology, E1 repeated or nested direct ecology, E2 locally inferred or filtered network, E3 target layer extracted from a broader bounded food web, M metaweb, or X enrichment only. Only E0/E1 form the direct-data layer.

Represent interactions in a canonical long table and distinguish observed positive, sampled zero, structural zero, not sampled, and unknown states. Generate matrices as deterministic views rather than independently edited canonical objects.

For each qualifying binary plant-by-herbivore matrix B, compute C = transpose(B) times B. Store host breadth from the diagonal separately and write only positive off-diagonal shared-host pairs as potential-competition edges.

Run deterministic reconciliation, orientation, hierarchy, duplicate, taxonomy, projection, and cross-format checks. Human reconstruction and independent second review remain explicit release gates rather than being silently inferred from automated tests.

Imported the exact version of this upstream dataset as a distinct source-derived component. Source semantics and verbatim taxon names were retained; all filtering, boundary decisions, and matrix transformations are recorded in derivations.csv.
